6-1. General. The subdivider shall provide all public improvements as required by this ordinance and by applicable city specifications and requirements.
6-1.1. The design of all minimum improvements shall be under the direction of an engineer registered in the State of Georgia, and all plans shall bear his seal.
6-1.2. A certificate of approval from the commissioner of health shall accompany all water and sewer plans.
6-2. Curbs and gutter. The subdivider may install curb and gutter in accordance with the requirements of section 5-6.13.
6-3. Monuments/pins. The subdivider shall provide, through the licensed surveyor, the setting of all reinforced concrete monuments and pins. The reinforced concrete monuments shall be four inches in diameter or square, 30 inches long with a flat top. The top of each monument shall be set flush with the ground. Said monuments shall be set within each block of the subdivision and shall be located along the longest interior straightaway; a minimum of four per block shall be installed as shown on the approved plat. Pins, a minimum of 15 inches long and one-half inch in diameter (metallic material type to be listed on plat) shall be placed along the exterior boundary and interior lot intersection except where concrete monuments are to be located, on each street corner, points of curvature in each street at all points where the street lines intersect the exterior boundary of the subdivision, and where such corners lie within a stream meander (in which case reference pins shall be placed on the bank of the stream). The pin shall be set a minimum of two inches under the ground. The top of the concrete monument shall contain a metal plate or metal rod, which shall be scored in such a manner that will properly and accurately identify the location.
6-4. Water supply and sanitary sewerage.
6-4.1. Every lot of a proposed subdivision shall be supplied with adequate water and sanitary facilities, which shall require the approval of the commissioner of health. Where existing water and sewer mains are in the street, but no services to the proposed lots, the subdivider shall have the services installed. Where public water and sanitary sewerage is available through extensions, the subdivider shall assure that every lot of the subdivision shall be provided with said public facilities in accordance with applicable city specifications.
6-4.2. Minimum Improvements: Standard fire hydrants of a type specified by the City of Quitman in the construction specifications shall be installed as a part of the water distribution system within a subdivision (existing or new) for single-family dwellings. A fire hydrant shall be located at each intersection and additional hydrant or hydrants installed where the distance between intersections exceeds five hundred (500) feet. In no case shall hydrants be spaced greater than five hundred (500) feet and shall be sized to have flow of seven hundred fifty (750) g.p.m. (gallons per minute) when adequate flow and pressure is available to the point of connection for the subdivision to the city system.
In multifamily and residential professional districts, fire hydrants shall be installed so that the distance from fire hydrants to the driveway entrance nearest the front of the building shall not exceed two hundred fifty (250), feet, with a total distance not to exceed five hundred (500) feet, with a total distance not to exceed five hundred (500) feet to the extreme back of the building by way of driveways. [As] an option, provided automatic sprinklers are installed according to N.F.P.A. regulations, the spacing of hydrants may be increased to three hundred fifty (350) feet to the driveway entrance nearest the front of the building, provided the total distance does not exceed seven hundred (700) feet to the extreme back of the building by way of driveways.
In light industrial, heavy industrial, central business and general business districts and any facility which handles or uses flammable or hazardous materials, hydrants shall be installed within three hundred (300) feet to the midpoint of the structure and equally spaced thereafter, not to exceed three hundred (300) feet between hydrants and the extreme rear of the building. The distance shall be measured along the line traveled by the fire truck. In the following zoning districts, hydrants shall be sized to have a flow capacity of not less than one thousand (1,000) g.p.m. (gallons per minute) when adequate flow and pressure is available to the point of connection for the subdivision to the city system: L-I, HI, GB and CBD. As an option, provided automatic sprinklers are installed according to N.F.P.A. requirements, the spacing of hydrants may be increased from three hundred (300) feet to five hundred (500) feet.
Distance between fire hydrants shall be as specified unless fire department operations would otherwise allow increased spacing. Actual location of fire hydrants shall be the responsibility of the fire chief or his representative.
6-4.3. The entire cost of extending water and sewer lines and their associated services within the subdivision shall be borne by the developer.
6-5. Sidewalks. (Reserved)
6-6. Street paving. The subdivider shall provide paved streets in accordance with this ordinance and applicable city specifications.
6-7. Stormwater drainage. The subdivider shall provide adequate stormwater drainage in accordance with these regulations and applicable city specifications. Where drainage conditions dictate, open ditches shall be paved. The subdivider shall also provide for adequate drainage of springs or other groundwater drainage.
6-8. Utilities. The installation of utilities shall be as follows:
6-8.1. Communication Distribution Systems: All communication distribution systems installed solely for the purpose of extending communications service within a development and within the property limits of such development shall be placed as directed by the staff development review committee.
6-8.2. Electric Power Distribution Systems: All electric distribution systems installed solely for the purpose of extending electric service to a development and within the property limits of such development shall be placed as directed by the staff development review committee.
6-8.3. Easements: Developers shall allocate necessary easements with future maintenance access.
6-8.4. Location of Underground Installations: The plans submitted to the city engineer will set forth the anticipated location of all underground installations. Location approval or acknowledgement by the owners of the underground installations shall be submitted.
6-9. Streetlighting. The general standard of residential streetlighting for Quitman, Georgia, is as follows:
6-9.1. Overhead Electrical Distribution: Residential lighting will be provided at intersections, dead-end streets or courts with a maximum spacing not to exceed five hundred (500) feet for straight streets, provided spacing shall be reduced as conditions indicate for curved streets or irregular contours so as to provide adequate lighting. Luminaries are to be twenty-eight-foot mounted on existing utility distribution poles and of an approved type mercury unit of approximately seven thousand (7,000) lumen.
6-9.2. Underground Electrical Distribution: Residential lighting will be provided at intersections, dead ends, or courts with a maximum spacing of four hundred (400) feet for straight streets, provided spacing shall be reduced as conditions indicate for curved streets or irregular contours so as to provide adequate lighting. Luminaries shall be top mounted on sixteen-foot (approximate) ornamental metal poles of an approved type mercury unit of approximately seven thousand (7,000) lumen.
6-9.3. Cost of Installation: In order to partially defray the cost of installation of streetlighting, the developer shall be required to pay a lump sum fee to the City of Quitman for each streetlight required under the provisions of this ordinance. The fees for streetlights will be as outlined on the current City of Quitman fee schedule.
Before the minimum improvements are accepted by the city, a check payable to the City of Quitman must be furnished for the total cost of the streetlights as determined above and as described in the streetlight layout plan.
6-9.4. Actions Prior to Construction: In order that the expense outlined herein may be ascertained and understood prior to commencement of construction, the developer or his engineer will confer with the city engineer and mark on the plans the approximate location for each fixture.
6-9.5. Location of Underground Installations: The plans submitted to the city engineer will set forth the exact location of all underground installations.
6-10. Buffer strips. The subdivider shall provide adequate buffer strips which consist of plantings and/or visual blinds as detailed in this ordinance.
6-11. Street signs. The developer shall pay for street signs necessitated by his subdivision as outlined in the current City of Quitman fee schedule. These fees shall be paid to the City of Quitman prior to the city manager's release of the plat for recording. Signs shall be installed by the city.
6-12. Installation of improvements. No grading, paving, or construction of any required improvements shall be permitted until the final plat and improvements plan of the subdivision has been approved by the city commission.
994:
7-1. Completion of improvements. Before the plat is signed by the Chairman of the Quitman City Commission, all developers shall be required to complete, in accordance with this ordinance and to the satisfaction of the Quitman City Manager, all minimum improvements as required by section [article] VI of this ordinance, specified on the final plat, and as approved by the planning commission, and to dedicate same to the City of Quitman.
7-1.1. In lieu of completion of the minimum improvements as required under this ordinance prior to recording of the final plat, the developer may post an irrevocable letter of credit or a performance bond. This instrument shall be made payable upon demand to the Quitman Board of Commissioners to ensure the completion of the required minimum improvements and shall be in an amount of not less than one hundred ten (110) percent of the estimated cost of all required minimum improvements. Cost estimates shall be prepared by the subdivider's professional engineer, and shall be subject to the review and approval of the city manager.
7-1.2. Bonds and/or cash posted pursuant to this alternative shall be released after formal acceptance of improvements by the city commission.
7-2. Acceptance. Upon written notification of completion of minimum improvements, the city manager within 30 days after such notice accept or reject, in writing, the completed improvements stating the deficiencies, if any.
7-2.1. The required minimum improvements shall not be accepted unless they conform to this ordinance and officially adopted city specifications.
7-3. Guarantee. The subdivider shall guarantee to the city, for a period of one year, after completion and acceptance of the improvement, all material and workmanship going into such improvement. The subdivider shall post bond with the city, conditioned upon the faithful performance of such guaranty. The guaranty shall be secured in the form of a bond, certified check or an irrevocable letter of credit, payable upon demand to the Quitman Board of Commissioners. Such guaranty and bond shall be posted prior to approval by the city of the subdivision plat. This guaranty shall be in the amount of 20 percent of the total improvements cost.
7-4. Recording of plat. Upon acceptance of all improvements installed by the developer and posting of the required guarantee, the office of the Quitman [City] Manager shall release the final plat for recording. Said plat shall be returned to the zoning administrator, who shall record said plat in a timely manner and distribute appropriate copies thereof in accordance with the directives of section 4-3.12.
7-5. Duration and release of guarantee. Bonds and/or cash posted pursuant to section 7-3 of this ordinance shall be released or returned at such time as the improvements guaranteed thereby have received final inspection after the guaranty period.
995:
8-1. Violations.
8-1.1. It shall be unlawful to convey or improve property by the construction of buildings on lots of any land subdivision which has not been approved and recorded as provided in this ordinance, except those parcels recorded prior to the effective date of this ordinance [June 4, 1991].
8-1.2. It shall be unlawful to record a subdivision plat or once recorded, to make any changes thereon whatsoever which have not been approved by the city commission, planning commission, city engineer, and the commissioner of health in accordance with the provisions of this ordinance.
8-1.3. Each Day's Violation a Separate Offense. After due notice has been given, each and every day's violation of any provision of this ordinance shall constitute a separate offense.
8-2. Violation and penalty. Any person who violates any provision of this subdivision ordinance shall, upon conviction in recorder's court, be penalized by the imposition of a fine not exceeding five hundred dollars ($500.00) per day and/or imprisonment in the city jail for a period not greater than 60 days.
996:
9-1. Effect of invalidity of part of resolution [ordinance]. Should any section or provision of this ordinance be decided by the courts to be invalid, such decision shall not affect the validity of this ordinance as a whole or any other part thereof.
9-2. Conflict with other laws. All ordinances or parts of ordinances in conflict herewith are hereby repealed.
9-3. Amendment. The city commission shall have the authority to amend this ordinance after a public hearing thereon. Notice of the time and place of such public hearing shall be published in a newspaper of general circulation in the City of Quitman at least 15 days prior to such meetings.

In cases of undue hardship under this ordinance, any property owner may petition the planning commission for a variance, and where the planning commission concurs, it will prepare and send to the city commissioners a recommendation for a variance when considered necessary and equitable. In case the planning commission fails to concur, the property owner may appeal to the city commissioners for relief. All variance requests will require a public hearing in the same manner as an amendment. None of the items listed in article VII, "Minimum Improvements," of this ordinance shall be subject to variance.

998: In pursuance of authority conferred by law, the city government of Quitman, Georgia, does ordain and enact into the law the following articles and sections.
999: The purpose of these regulations is to promote the health, safety, morals, convenience, order, prosperity, or the general welfare for the City of Quitman, Georgia; lessen congestion in the streets; secure safety from fire, panic, and other dangers; provide adequate light and air; prevent the overcrowding of land; avoid undue concentration of population; facilitate the adequate provision of transportation, water, sewage, schools, parks and other public requirements; conserve the value of buildings and encourage the most appropriate use of land and buildings throughout the city.
1000: This ordinance shall be known and be cited as "The Zoning Ordinance of the City of Quitman, Georgia."
1001: For the purpose of this ordinance, certain terms and words are hereby defined. Except as specifically defined herein, all words have their customary definition.
1002:
Words used in the present tense include the future tense. Words used in the singular include the plural, and words in the plural include the singular.
The word "shall" is always mandatory.
The word "person" includes a firm, association, organization, trust, company, or corporation as well as an individual.
The word "lot" includes the word "plot" or "parcel."
The word "building" includes the word "structure."
The word "used" or "occupied," as applied to any land or building, shall be construed to include the words "intended, arranged, or designated to be used or occupant."
The word "map" or "zoning map" mean the Official Zoning Map of the City of Quitman.
1003:
The following terms or words are hereby specifically defined:
4-2.1 Accessory Use or Building: The use or building customarily incidental and subordinate to the principal use or building located on the same lot with such principal use or building.
4-2.2 Building: Any structure, except a trailer, intended for shelter, housing, or enclosure of persons, animals, or chattels.
4-2.3 Building, Principal: A building in which is conducted the main or principal use of the lot on which said building is located.
4-2.4 Dwelling: A building designated or used for permanent living quarters for one or more families or individuals.
4-2.5 Dwelling Unit: One or more rooms with kitchen facilities designed as a unit for occupancy by one family for cooking, living, and sleeping purposes.
4-2.6 Family: One or more persons occupying a premises and living as a single housekeeping unit, as distinguished from a group occupying a boarding house, lodging house, hotel, or fraternity or sorority house.
4-2.7 Floor Area, Gross: The total number of square feet of floor area in a building determined by horizontal measurements between the exterior faces of walls, excluding basement area, porches, carports, or garages.
4-2.8 Home Occupation: An occupation or profession for gain or support conducted only by members of the family residing on the premises and conducted entirely within the principal or accessory buildings, provided that the total floor area used for such purposes does not equal more than 25% of the floor area of the principal building. (See Section 5-16)
4-2.9 Junk Yard: Use of property for outdoor storage, keeping, abandonment, sale, or resale of junk including scrap metal, rags, paper or other scrap materials, used lumber, salvaged house wrecking and structural steel, materials and equipment, or for the dismantling, demolition, or abandonment of automobiles or other vehicles or machinery or parts thereof.
4-2.10 Lot: A parcel of land being occupied or capable of being occupied by one or more buildings, including accessory buildings incidental to them, and including such open spaces as required by such [this] ordinance.
4-2.11 Lot of Record: A lot which is part of a subdivision recorded in the office of the clerk of the Superior Court, or a parcel of land described by metes and bounds, the description of which has been so recorded.
4-2.12 Lot, Width: The distance between the side lot lines, measured along the front yard setback line as established by this ordinance, or if no setback is established, the horizontal distance between the side lot lines measured along the street right-of-way line.
4-2.13 Non-Conforming Use: A building, structure, or use of land existing at the time of the enactment of this ordinance which does not conform to the regulations of the district in which it is located.
4-2.14 Nursery School: An agency, organization, or individual providing daytime care of four or more children not related by blood or marriage or not the legal wards or foster children of the attendant adult.
4-2.15 Setback: The distance from the center line of the street to the nearest point of the building.
4-2.16 Street: A public way for vehicular traffic which affords a primary means of access to abutting property.
4-2.17 Structure: Anything constructed or erected with a fixed location on or in the ground, or attached to something having a fixed location on the ground. Among other things, structures include buildings, mobile homes, billboards, swimming pools, and fall-out shelters but does not include walls or fences, excepting signs or billboards of less than 48 square feet in area on one side.
4-2.18 Trailer (Mobile Home): Any trailer, vehicle, or similar portable structure mounted on wheels, or designed for mounting on wheels, including structural additions, except camping type trailers parked and unoccupied. Such unit shall be considered a mobile home whether or not the wheels have been removed and whether or not on a temporary or permanent foundation. (See Section 5-17)
4-2.19 Yard, Front: An open unoccupied space on the same lot with the principal building, between the front line of the principal building and the front line of the lot, and extending the full width of the lot. (See Article VI)
4-2.20 Yard, Rear: An open unoccupied space except for an accessory structure on the same lot with the principal building, between the rear line of the building and the rear line of the lot and extending the full width of the lot. (See Article VI)
4-2.21 Proposed Zoning Change: A request by a party for a change in the zoning ordinance for the city of Quitman which may result in:
(a) The adoption of a zoning ordinance;
(b) The adoption of an amendment to a zoning ordinance which changes the text of a zoning ordinance; or
(c) The adoption of an amendment to a zoning ordinance which rezones property from one zoning classification to another.
4-2.22 Apartment Complex: An apartment complex is defined as any building or portion thereof used as a multiple dwelling for the purpose for providing three or more separate dwelling units whether separated by a fire wall or not which may or may not share a common means of egress or other common facilities, including but not limited to a common yard, recreational facilities, driveway, parking lot, central courtyard, or other facilities of similar nature.
(Ord. No. 303, § 1, 1-7-1985; Ord. No. 325, § 3, 10-6-1986; Ord. No. 394, A, 1-8-1991)
1005: Any use of any building or structure or land existing at the time of the enactment of this ordinance may be continued even though such use does not conform with the provisions of this ordinance, except that a non-conforming use shall not be changed to another non-conforming use or re-established after discontinuance of more than one year; or extended except in conformity with this ordinance; or rebuilt, altered, or repaired after damage exceeding 75% of the replacement cost at the time of destruction. (See Section 4-2.13).
1006:
The following off-street parking requirements shall apply to all zoning districts except the CBD (Central Business District). Off-street vehicle storage or standing space (each space to be ten feet wide, 20 feet deep in addition to adequate access drives and maneuvering area) shall be provided on any lot where any of the following uses are hereafter established. Such parking area shall have direct vehicular access to a street or alley and shall contain at least the number of parking spaces as set forth below:
5-2.1 Residences: One parking space for each family dwelling unit.
5-2.2 Rooming Houses, Tourist Homes, Motels, and Hotels: One parking space for each rental unit.
5-2.3 Churches, Theaters, Auditoriums, or Other Places of Public Assembly: One parking space for every three hundred (300) square feet of floor area, or one space for each four seats or facilities available for patron use, whichever is greatest.
5-2.4 Indoor Recreation Establishments, Clubs, Lodges or Commercial Schools: One parking space for every three hundred (300) square feet of floor area, or one space for each four seats or facilities available for patron use, whichever is greatest.
5-2.5 Kindergarten and Nursery Schools: One parking space for each employee plus a suitable area for safe and convenient loading of students.
5-2.6 Trailer Park: One parking space for each trailer stall.
5-2.7 Retail Trade and Services: One parking space for each two hundred (200) square feet devoted to trade or service activity, plus one parking space for each vehicle used directly in the conduct of the enterprise.
5-2.8 Office, Professional, or Public Building: One parking space for each three hundred (300) square feet of floor area.
5-2.9 Hospitals: One parking space for each two beds intended for patients.
5-2.10 Warehousing, Wholesale Trade, Manufacturing, or Industrial Establishments: One parking space for each two employees plus one parking space for each vehicle used directly in the conduct of the enterprise.
1007:
Industrial, wholesale, and retail operations shall provide loading space as follows:
5-3.1 Spaces Appropriate to Functions: Off-street loading spaces shall be provided as appropriate to the functions and scope of operation of individual or groups of buildings and uses.
5-3.2 Design of Loading Spaces: Off-street loading spaces shall be designed and constructed so that all maneuvering to park and unpark vehicles for loading and unloading can take place entirely within the property lines of the premises. Loading spaces shall be provided so as not to interfere with the free, normal movement of vehicles and pedestrians on public rights-of-way.
5-3.3 Off-Street Loading Spaces: Where off-street truck loading and unloading space is required such space shall be at least ten feet wide and 24 feet in length.
1008: If vehicle parking or storage space required cannot be reasonably provided on the same lot on which the principal use is conducted, such space may be provided on other property provided such property lies within two hundred fifty (250) feet of the main entrance of the principal use.
1009: No building or structure shall hereafter be used or occupied and no building or structure or part thereof shall be erected, constructed, reconstructed, moved, subdivided, or altered except in conformity with the regulations herein specified. (See Sections 9-2 and 9-3)
1010: No building shall hereafter be erected, constructed, or altered so as to exceed the height limit, or so as to accommodate or house a greater number of families than required or specified by the regulations herein for the district in which it is located.
1011: No building shall hereafter be erected, reconstructed, constructed, or altered to have a narrower or smaller front, side or rear yard than herein required, and off-street parking spaces shall not be reduced below the minimum number as required herein. (See Article VI and Section 5-2)
1012: No lot shall hereafter be created except in conformity with the regulations herein specified; and no lot shall be reduced in size so that lot width, size of yard, lot area, or any other requirement of this ordinance is not maintained.
1013: No building shall hereafter be constructed on a lot which does not have at least 30 feet of frontage on a publicly dedicated, publicly accepted, and publicly maintained street.
1014: Within residential districts only, no more than one principal building with its customary accessory buildings may occupy or be constructed upon any lot of record. (See Section 4-2.11 and Section 4-2.3)
1015: On a corner lot where the main entrance into a residence is facing a side yard, it shall be permissible for purposes of this ordinance to construe the residence to be fronting on the street other than that street which said entrance faces, and side and rear yard requirements may be provided accordingly. If a building is constructed on a through lot having frontage on two roads not at an intersection, a setback from each road shall be provided equal to the front yard requirement for the district in which the lot is located.
1016:
When a building is proposed on a lot and when on either or both lots which adjoin such lot at the street right-of-way line there exists a principal building which does not conform to the setback requirements of this ordinance, and the Board of Zoning Appeals finds that because of the width and shape of the lot it would impose an unnecessary hardship on the owner if the rigid requirements of this ordinance were followed, the Board may allow the required setback for such building to be as follows:
(1) where only one said adjoining lot contains a principle building with a non-conforming setback, the setback shall be the computed average of (a) the normal setback requirement with (b) the nonconforming setback; or
(2) where both adjoining lots contain a principle building each with a nonconforming setback, the minimum setback shall be the computed average of the two nonconforming setbacks. (See Section 10-6.3)
1017: If two or more adjoining and vacant lots of record with continuous frontage are in a single ownership any time after the adoption of this ordinance and such lots individually are less than the lot width requirements for the district in which they are located, such groups of lots shall together be considered as a single lot or shall be grouped into several lots of minimum permitted size; the resulting lot or lots shall be subject to the dimensional requirements of this ordinance. (See Section 4-2.11)
1018: Except as set forth in Section 5-13, any lot of record at any [the] time of the adoption of this ordinance which does not meet the minimum lot width and/or lot area requirements herein provided, may be used as a building site for a single-family residence, provided the required yard setbacks are maintained. (See Section 4-2.11)
1019: Architectural features such as cornices, eaves, steps, gutters, and fire escapes may project not more than three feet beyond any required setback line, except where such projections would obstruct driveways which are or may be used for access for service and/or emergency vehicles.
1020:
A home occupation as defined by this ordinance shall be governed by the following requirements: (See Section 4-2.8)
a. Only residents of the dwelling may be engaged in the home occupation.
b. The home occupation shall be clearly incidental to the residential use of the dwelling, and shall not change the essential residential character of the building.
c. No display of products shall be visible from the street, and only products produced on the premises may be sold on the premises.
d. Use of the building for this purpose shall not exceed 25% of one floor of the principle building.
e. No internal or external alterations inconsistent with the residential use of the building shall be permitted.
f. The occupational [occupation] shall not constitute a nuisance in the neighborhood.
g. No accessory buildings or outside storage shall be used in connection with the occupation.
h. Instruction in music and similar subjects shall be limited to two students at a time.
i. Vehicles used primarily as passenger vehicles only shall be permitted in connection with the conduct of the customary home occupation.
j. No more than three non-transient guests may be boarded at any one time as a customary home occupation.
k. The following and similar uses shall be considered home occupations: addressing service, art instructor, beauty shop, dentist, doctor, drafting, dressmaking, insurance agent, manufacturing agent, massage parlor, music teacher, notary public, photography, real estate agent, tax consultant.
1021:
Trailer parks are allowed within R-P and G-B districts provided the following requirements are met: (See Section 5-2.6)
a. The minimum size shall be three acres; and
b. The park shall have minimum side yards of 15 feet and a front yard at least 20 feet greater than that required for other uses permitted in the district; and
c. Each trailer shall be connected to water, sewerage, and electrical utilities; and,
d. The minimum lot area per trailer shall be no less than two thousand four hundred (2,400) square feet with a minimum stall width of 40 feet where served by public water and sewers. The lot shall not contain less than four thousand (4,000) square feet of lot area per trailer where trailers will be served by septic tanks; and
e. The minimum distance between any two trailers or between any trailer and any other building in the park shall be 20 feet; and
f. A 20 foot drive properly drained, shall serve each trailer lot and be drained so as to prevent damage to adjoining property, public or private; and
g. Each trailer lot shall be clearly defined by means of concrete, steel, or iron pipe markers placed at all corners; and
h. At least two hundred (200) square feet per trailer lot not to be a part of required trailer stalls, shall be provided in one or more locations for community playground and recreation purposes; and
i. No trailer park shall be occupied by a greater number of trailers than that authorized in the approved building and occupancy permits. No trailer park shall be enlarged or extended unless a separate building permit and a separate occupancy permit have been issued; and
j. Access to all trailer parks shall be limited to a major or secondary street, as designated on the Thoroughfare Plan for the City.
1022:
In emergency and hardship situations a special exception may be granted by the Board of Commissioners of the City of Quitman by majority vote upon written application directly to said board to allow the temporary use of a mobile home or other type of movable dwelling facility including travel trailers as a residence in the City of Quitman for a period not to exceed 120 days from date of issuance, provided the following conditions and/or restrictions are complied with:
(a) Hardship or emergency situation shall be limited to the destruction or partial destruction (to the extent that same is rendered uninhabitable in the opinion of the building inspector of the City of Quitman), of an owner occupied single-family residence by fire, wind, flood, earthquake or other act of God.
(b) Said residence must be the principal residence of the owner/occupier and an affidavit to that effect shall accompany the application to the Board of Commissioners for the special exception.
(c) The special exception shall be limited to the placement of a mobile home or travel trailer upon the same lot occupied by the destroyed or uninhabitable structure by the causes listed in paragraph (a).
(d) The special exception permit shall be limited to a period of 120 days from the date of issuance or for so long as the reconstruction or rehabilitation of the residence in question takes whichever period is shorter. Under no circumstances shall a mobile home or travel trailer be allowed to remain in place in an area under this ordinance [section] for a period in excess of 120 days.
(e) Each applicant for this special exception must present proof of his or her financial ability to rebuild or repair said residence within the 120-day period of time and said proof shall accompany the application for said special exception and shall be in such form as may be from time to time determined by the Board of Commissioners of the City of Quitman in its sole discretion.
(f) The written consent of all land owners within a two-hundred-foot radius of the property in question if said property is not within a subdivision in the City of Quitman[;] and if said property is within a subdivision in the City of Quitman, said application shall be accompanied by a written consent of all owners of property within said subdivision.
It is the intention of the commission that this ordinance [section] be interpreted and applied only in very limited cases and only to prevent severe hardships on residents of the city in emergency situations.
In determining whether to issue an exception under this section, alternate housing availability shall be a major determining factor to be considered by the Board of Commissioners.

1027:
Where uncertainties exist with respect to the boundaries of any aforesaid districts as shown on the Quitman Zoning Map, the following rules shall apply:
7-3.1 Where the district boundaries are indicated as approximately following the center lines of streets or highways, right-of-way lines, such center lines, street lines, or highway right-of-way lines shall be construed to be such boundaries.
7-3.2 Where district boundaries are indicated on the Quitman Zoning Map as being set back from a street, road, highway, railroad, stream, or river, and parallel thereto, then such district boundaries unless otherwise specifically indicated, shall be construed as being at the scaled distance from the center line of such street, road, highway, railroad, stream, or river and as being parallel thereto.
7-3.3 Boundaries indicated as approximately following platted lot lines shall be construed as following such lot lines.
7-3.4 Where a district boundary line as appearing on the Quitman Zoning Map divides a lot in a single ownership at the time of this enactment, district requirements of the least restrictive portion of such lot shall be deemed to apply to the whole thereof, provided that such extensions shall not include any part of such lot more than thirty-five (35) feet beyond the district boundary line.

1037: The office of Zoning Administrator of the City of Quitman, Georgia, is hereby established. The duties of the Zoning Administrator shall include inspecting premises, issuing building permits and certificates of occupancy for uses and buildings, and assuring that all such buildings and uses are in accordance with the requirements of this ordinance.
1038:
Building permits shall be issued in accordance with the following provisions:
9-2.1 Building Permit Required: It shall be unlawful to commence construction, moving, or alteration of any building until the Zoning Administrator has issued a building permit for such work and such permit is posted in view of the street on the premises where the building, moving or alteration is to take place.
9-2.2 Issuance of the Building Permit: In applying to the Zoning Administrator for a building permit, the applicant shall submit two copies of a dimensional sketch or a to-scale plan signed by the owner or his authorized agent, indicating the shape, size, and location of the lot to be built upon and the shape, size, height, use, and location of the buildings to be erected, demolished, altered, or moved and of any buildings already on the lot, the number of dwelling units the building is designed to accommodate (if any), the setback lines of buildings on adjoining lots, and such other information concerning the lot or adjoining lots as may be essential for determining whether the provisions of this ordinance are being observed. If the proposed excavation, filling, construction, or movement set forth in said sketch or plan are in conformity with the provisions of this ordinance and other ordinances of the City of Quitman, Georgia, then in force, the Zoning Administrator shall sign and return one copy of the sketch plan to the applicant and shall issue a building permit upon payment of the required fee. The Zoning Administrator shall retain one copy of the building permit and one copy of the sketch or plan.
9-2.3 Refusal of Building Permit: If the sketch of plan submitted describes work which does not conform to the requirements of this ordinance, the Zoning Administrator shall not issue a building permit but shall return one copy of the sketch or plan to the applicant along with the refusal in writing. Such refusal shall state the reasons therefor and shall cite portions of this ordinance with which the submitted sketch or plan does not comply. The Zoning Administrator shall retain one copy of the sketch or plan and one copy of the refusal.
9-2.4 Time Limitations: Any building permit issued shall become invalid unless the work authorized by it shall have been commenced within six months of its date of issue, or if the work authorized by it is suspended or abandoned for a period of one year.
1039:
A certificate of occupancy shall be issued by the Zoning Administrator in accordance with the following provisions:
9-3.1 Certificate of Occupancy Required: A certificate of occupancy issued by the Zoning Administrator is required in advance of occupancy or use of:
(a) a building hereafter erected.
(b) a building hereafter altered so as to affect the height; or the side, front, or rear yards.
(c) any building or premises where a change in the type of occupancy or use will occur.
9-3.2 Issuance of Certificate of Occupancy: Upon payment of any required fees, the Zoning Administrator shall sign and issue a certificate of occupancy if the proposed use of land or building as stated on the certificate of occupancy, as signed thereto by the owner or his appointed agent, is found to conform to the applicable provisions of this ordinance and if the building, as finally constructed, complies with the sketch or plan submitted for the building permit. One copy of all certificates of occupancy issued which contain a statement of the intended use of the applicable property signed by the owner or his agent shall be kept on file in the office of the Zoning Administrator.
9-3.3 Denial of Certificate of Occupancy: A certificate of occupancy shall not be issued unless the proposed use of a building or land conforms to the applicable provisions of this ordinance, or unless the building, as finally constructed, complies with the sketch or plan upon which the building permit was issued.
1040: It shall be the duty of the Zoning Administrator to keep a record of all building permits and certificates of occupancy issued, with a notation of all special conditions involved. He shall file and safely keep copies of all sketches and plans submitted, and the same shall form a part of the records of his office and shall be available for use by the City Commission, Board of Zoning Appeals, Planning Commission, and Officials of the City of Quitman, Georgia, and the general public.
1041: Any person violating any provision of this ordinance shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction shall be punished for each offense according to law. Each day such violation continues shall be deemed a separate offense.
1042: In case any building is erected, constructed, reconstructed, altered, repaired, converted, or maintained, or any building or land is used in violation of this ordinance, the Zoning Administrator, or any appropriate city attorney, or any person who would be damaged by such violation, in addition to other remedies, may institute injunction, mandamus, or other appropriate action or proceedings to stop the violation in the case of each such building or use of land.
1044:
10-1.1 Appointment and Term of Office: The Board of Zoning Appeals of the City of Quitman, Georgia, is hereby established. Said Board shall consist of three members appointed by the City Commission for overlapping terms of three years. Initial appointment shall be as follows: one member, for one year; one member for two years; and one member for three years; each successive appointment shall be for three years. Any vacancy in the membership shall be filled for the unexpired term in the same manner as the initial appointment. Members may be removed for cause by the appointing authority upon written charges and after a public hearing. No member shall hold any public office or position, except that one member may also be a member of the Planning Commission. The Board of Zoning Appeals shall adopt rules in accordance with the provisions of this ordinance for the conduct of its affairs.
10-1.2 Compensation: The Board members shall receive no compensation for their service except that they shall be reimbursed for out-of-pocket expenditures made in connection with their duties.
1045: The Board shall elect one of its members as Chairman, who shall serve for one year or until he is reelected or his successor is elected. The Board of Appeals shall appoint a secretary who may be an officer of the City of Quitman, or of the Planning Commission. The Board shall have authority to adopt rules of procedure. Meetings of the Board shall be held at the call of the Chairman, or in his absence the acting Chairman. The Chairman, or in his absence the acting Chairman, may administer oaths and compel the attendance of witnesses by subpoena. The Board shall keep minutes of its proceedings, showing the vote of each member upon each question, or if absent or failing to vote, indicating such fact and shall keep records of its examinations and other official actions, all of which shall be immediately filed in the office of said Board and shall be a public record. The decisions of the Board shall be by resolution, which resolution shall contain a statement of the grounds of its decision or action. The full text of the resolution shall be sent to the appellant. No appeal requesting the same relief in regard to the same property shall be received or heard by the Board for a period of 12 months following the date of said resolution, except that this limitation shall not affect the right of said Board to grant a rehearing as provided in the rules of procedure adopted by said Board. All hearings shall be open to the public.
1046: The Zoning Administrator shall provide such technical, administrative, and clerical assistance and office space as is required by the Board to carry out its function under the provisions of these regulations.
1047:
10-4.1 Who May Appeal: Appeals to the Board may be taken by any person aggrieved or by any officer, department, board, or bureau of the governing authority affected by any decision of the Zoning Administrator. Such appeals shall be filed no later than 30 days after the date of notification of the decision appealed from, by filing with the Zoning Administrator and with the Board a notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof. The Zoning Administrator shall forthwith transmit to the Board all the papers constituting the record upon which the action appealed from was taken.
10-4.2 Legal Proceedings Stayed: An appeal stays all legal proceedings in furtherance of the action appealed from, unless the Zoning Administrator certifies to the Board, after the notice of appeal shall have been filed with him, that by reason of acts stated in the certificate a stay would, in his opinion, cause imminent peril to life and property. In such a case, proceedings shall not be stayed otherwise than by restraining order which may be granted by the Board or by a court of record on application, on notice to the Zoning Administrator, and on due cause shown.
10-4.3 Presentation of Evidence: The appellant, and any public agency, or private individual shall be entitled to present evidence on matters before the Board; and said Board may request technical service, advice, data, or factual evidence from the Planning Commission, and the governing authority for assistance in reaching decisions.
10-4.4 Extent of Board of Appeal's Power: The Board may, in conformity with the provisions of these regulations, reverse or affirm, wholly or partly, or may modify the order, requirement, decision, or determination of the Zoning Administrator, and to that end shall have all the powers of the Zoning Administrator. The Board may direct the issuance of a permit. It shall be the duty of the Zoning Administrator to carry out the decisions of the Board.
1048:
10-5.1 Notice of Hearing Shall Be Given: Before making its decision on a special exception, or on a request for a variance, or on any other matter within the Board's purview, said Board shall hold a public hearing thereon. At least 15 days notice of the time and place of such hearing shall be sent to the appellant or petitioner by mail to his last known address, to the Planning Commission, to the Zoning Administrator, and to the owners of all properties either adjoining the property on which the hearing is concerned or situated directly across a public right-of-way from said property. Such notice shall contain the name of the appellant or petitioner, the date, time, and place set for the hearing, and a brief statement of the nature of the hearing.
10-5.2 Public Notice in Newspaper: The Board shall give public notice of the hearing in a newspaper published and circulated in Brooks County by advertisement published at least 15 days prior to the date of the public hearing.
10-5.3 Who May Appear: Any party may appear at the public hearing in person or by agent or attorney.
10-5.4 Time Limit on Board's Decision: The Board shall reach a decision following a public hearing within 30 days.
1049:
10-6.1 Appeals from Actions of the Zoning Administrator: The Board shall hear and decide upon appeals where it is alleged there is error in any order, requirement, decision, or determination made by the Zoning Administrator in the enforcement of these regulations.
10-6.2 Special Exceptions: The Board shall hear and decide upon special exceptions as authorized by this ordinance. The application to establish such use shall be approved on a finding by the Board of Appeals that:
(a) The proposed use will not be contrary to the purpose of this ordinance.
(b) The proposed use will not be detrimental to the use or development of adjacent properties or the general neighborhood nor affect adversely the health and safety of residents and workers.
(c) The proposed use will not constitute a nuisance or hazard because of the number of persons who will attend or use such facility, vehicular movement, noise or fumes generated, or type of physical activity.
(d) The proposed use will not be affected adversely by the existing uses, and the proposed use will be placed on a lot of sufficient size to satisfy the space requirements of said use.
(e) The parking and all development standards set forth for each particular use for which a permit may be granted have been met.
(f) Provided, that the Board of Zoning Appeals may impose or require such additional restriction and standards as may be necessary to protect the health and safety of workers and residents in the community, to protect the value and use of property in the general neighborhood; and provided, that wherever the Board of Zoning Appeals shall find, in the case of any permit granted pursuant to the provisions of these regulations, that any term, condition, or restrictions upon which such permit was granted are not being complied with, said Board shall rescind and revoke such permit after giving due notice to all parties concerned and granting full opportunity for a public hearing.
10-6.3 Request for a Variance: The Board may authorize upon appeal in specific cases such variance from the terms of these regulations as will not be contrary to the public interest where, owing to special conditions, a literal enforcement of the provisions of these regulations will, in an individual case, result in practical difficulty or unnecessary hardship, so that the spirit of these regulations shall be observed, public safety and welfare secured, and substantial justice done; provided, however, that a variance shall not be granted for a use of land or building or structure that is prohibited by this ordinance in the district in question. Such variance may be granted in an individual case upon finding by the Board that the following exists:
(a) there are extraordinary and exceptional conditions pertaining to the particular piece of property in question because of its size, shape, or topography; and
(b) the special conditions and circumstances existing are not a result of the action of the applicant; and
(c) the application of these regulations to this particular piece of property would create a practical difficulty or hardship; and
(d) such conditions are peculiar to the particular piece of property involved; and
(e) the variance requested is the minimum variance that will make possible the reasonable use of land, building or structure; and
(f) relief, if granted, would not cause substantial detriment to the public good or impair the purposes and intent of these regulations; provided, however, that no variance may be granted for a use of land or building or structure that is prohibited by this ordinance; and
(g) a literal interpretation of this ordinance would deprive the applicant of any rights that others in the same district are allowed; and
(h) provided, that the Board of Zoning Appeals may impose or require such additional restrictions and standards as may be necessary to protect the health and safety of workers and residents in the community, and to protect the value and use of property in the general neighborhood; and provided, that wherever the Board of Zoning Appeals shall find, in the case of any permit granted pursuant to the provisions of these regulations, that any of the terms, conditions, or restrictions upon which such permit was granted are not being complied with, said Board shall rescind and revoke such permit after giving due notice to all parties concerned and granting full opportunity for a public hearing.
10-6.4 Forms: Appeals shall be made on forms provided by the Zoning Administrator, and all information required on said forms shall be provided by the applicant. Forms shall be filed with the Board, and the appellant shall pay the Board for expense incidental to the appeal. No form shall be accepted by the Board unless it contains all pertinent information and is accompanied by a forty dollar ($40.00) fee, payable to the city, to defray expenses.
(Ord. No. 303, § 3, 1-7-1985)

1053:
These regulations, including the Quitman Zoning Map, may be amended by the City Commission on its own motion, on petition or on recommendation of the Planning Commission. 1054:
11-2.1 In the event of an initial zoning ordinance, update or major revisions of the zoning ordinance or a rezoning requested by the City, the Planning Commission shall, using all available resources and materials at its disposal, study the needs of the City and develop a draft zoning ordinance complete with appropriate specifications and conditions and, additionally, provide a Zoning Map of the City of Quitman to delineate zoned district boundaries, if the same is required.
11-2.2 Standards and Evaluation Form. The Planning Commission shall, whenever it reviews a proposed zoning change, evaluate each proposed change according to each of the standards listed below. The evaluation form listed in Appendix B-1 shall be completed by the Planning Commission for each proposed change. This shall be done prior to the Public Hearing required in Section 11-2.4. The standards are as follows:
(1) The existing land use and zoning classification of adjacent and nearby property.
(2) The possible creation of an isolated district unrelated to adjacent and nearby property.
(3) The extent to which property values of adjacent or nearby property may be diminished by the proposed zoning change.
(4) The population density pattern and the possible increase or overtaxing of the load on public facilities including, but not limited to, utilities and streets.
(5) The cost of the City of Quitman in providing, improving, increasing or maintaining public utilities, streets and public safety measures.
(6) The relative gain to the citizens of Quitman as compared to the hardship imposed upon the property owner.
(7) Whether there are substantial reasons why the property cannot be used in accordance with its existing zoning classification.
(8) The length of time the property has been vacant as zoned considered in the context of land development in the area in the vicinity of the property.
(9) The aesthetic effect of existing and future use of the property as if relates to the surrounding area.
(10) The extent to which the proposed zoning change will be consistent with the comprehensive plan of the Zoning Ordinance for the City of Quitman.
(11) Any other factors relevant to the balancing of interests in promoting the public health, safety, morality or general welfare of the Citizens of Quitman against the right of unrestricted use of property.
11-2.3 Review of Proposed Zoning Amendment with City Commission. The Planning Commission shall, after the completion of the proposed zoning amendment and its evaluation form, review the same with the City Commission. The City Commission shall make whatever changes, deletions or additions it desires necessary to make at this meeting and any changes made by the City Commission shall be incorporated into a final draft of the Zoning Ordinance for public inspection. The City Commission shall also set a time, date and location for a public hearing before the Planning Commission on the proposed zoning change.
11-2.4 Notice of Public Hearing. The Clerk of the City shall, after the meeting held pursuant to [section]11-2.3, prepare and cause to be published in the official organ for the City of Quitman a notice containing a summary of the proposed zoning change to be considered and the date, and place of the Public Hearing. Said Notice shall be published not less than 15 days nor more than forty-five (45) days prior to the hearing date.
11-2.5 Availability for Public Inspection. The City Clerk shall provide, for public inspection, copies of the proposed zoning ordinance and map, if required, and the evaluation form completed by the Planning Commission. Public inspection may be had during the normal business hours of the City Office from the date of the appearance of the public hearing notice until the day of the hearing.
11-2.6 Procedure and Conduct for the Public Hearing. The public hearing shall be convened at the time, date and location set forth in the public notice and shall be presided over by the Chairman of the Planning Commission. The Chairman shall state that the meeting will be held in accordance with Robert's Rules of Order and, further, shall state the following additional procedures:
(1) The Chairman must recognize an individual from the floor before he may speak. Upon being recognized, the individual shall give his name and address.
(2) The individual speaking will be allowed three minutes to express any opinion and make points on each separate element of the proposed zoning change which he wishes to address, with a maximum of 15 points allowed per individual. Additional individuals may be recognized by the Chairman in accordance with the aforementioned procedure to enunciate additional points of elements of the proposed zoning change. The Chairman may grant individuals additional time, if he so desires.
(3) The citizens in attendance will have the right to discuss all elements of the proposed zoning change that each individual wishes to address so long as the procedures set forth hereinabove are complied with.
(4) The Chairman shall, prior to all arguments on the proposed zoning change, review the proposed zoning change and evaluation sheet that has been previously prepared. The Secretary of the Planning Commission shall be made available to make notes of the proceedings.
11-2.7 Decision of the Planning Commission. The Planning Commission shall make a decision on the proposed zoning change within three days of the public hearing.
Should the Planning Commission elect to make a decision at the Public Hearing, the Chairman shall announce the Planning Commission's recommendation at the hearing and that its recommendation will be placed on the City Commission's agenda for the next regular monthly meeting for approval or disapproval. Within three business days of its decision, the Planning Commission shall have the minutes of the public hearing, the proposed zoning change and the evaluation form transmitted to the City Clerk so that it may be placed on the City Commission's agenda for the next regular monthly meeting. Not later than one day after the decision has been rendered by the Planning Commission, the decision shall be posted as a regular public notice at the City Hall.
(Ord. No. 325, § 2, 10-6-1986)
